name: Dialog Transcription
prompt_body:
Transcribe this medical dictation verbatim with speaker labels. The recording is a conversation between multiple physicians speaking in mixed Egyptian Colloquial Arabic and English (medical terminology plus casual code-switched English).

SPEAKER LABELING:
- Identify each distinct speaker by voice and label every turn. Use names if a speaker is clearly addressed by name in the audio (e.g., Dr. Sameh, Dr. Tarek); otherwise use generic consistent labels (Speaker 1, Speaker 2, …).
- Start each turn on a new line in the format:  **[Speaker]:** <their words>
- Keep the same label for the same voice throughout. When the speaker changes, start a new labeled line.
- If a speaker is uncertain or two voices overlap, mark as [Speaker ?] or [overlapping speech].

TRANSCRIPTION RULES (apply within each turn):
- Write all genuinely Arabic/colloquial speech in Arabic script (العربية), exactly as spoken — preserve the Egyptian dialect, do not standardize to formal Arabic.
- Write all medical, anatomical, pharmacological, and technical terms in English, even when embedded mid-sentence (e.g., ejection fraction, pulmonary artery reconstruction, unifocalization, Ebstein anomaly, ICU, CRP).
- Code-switched everyday English words: when a word is fundamentally English and merely pronounced with an Arabic accent — with no native Arabic meaning in that context — write it in English, NOT Arabic phonetic script (write "الـ pattern", "نـ focus", "impress them", "outcomes" — never "الباترن", "نفوكس", "إمبريس دم", "أوت كامز").
- Keep Arabic grammatical prefixes/particles (الـ، بـ، نـ، هـ، وـ) in Arabic when attached to an English word, but keep the English word in Latin script (e.g., "الـ next steps", "هنـ focus").
- Keep drug names, dosages, units, abbreviations, and acronyms in standard English/Latin form (e.g., 80 mg, BID, ECG, LVEF).
- Do not translate. Preserve the original language of every word as it was spoken.
- Spell English/medical terms with their correct standard spelling, even if pronounced with an accent.
- Output the labeled transcription only — no preamble, summary, or commentary.
